reasons: PRIMARY TEST IS ANTI-CONSERVATIVE FOR A VARIANCE-SELECTING RANKER. The pre-registered pass rule ('avg net > matched mean with one-sided p < 0.05 from 200 matched draws') places the rule's mean in the distribution of matched-portfolio means (idxsig/backtest.py _baseline, dist(): p = share of draws >= observed). That distribution's spread is sigma_matched/sqrt(n), while the rule's own mean has SE sigma_rule/sqrt(n). Whenever the rule picks names more volatile than their matched controls (coarse tercile matching, see next point), the nominal 5% test has a larger size under the null of equal means. Measured on the recorded runs (results/runs/*/trades.csv.gz vs random_draws.csv, SKIP_OVERLAP excluded): IDX 000401Z rule per-trade std 0.189, SE 0.0094 vs draw-mean SD 0.0061 -> implied size 14%; crypto 005732Z 0.349/0.0215 vs 0.0081 -> 27%; US 060443Z 0.346/0.0104 vs 0.0059 -> 18%; US fill-B 115656Z -> 23%; IDX FILL-C 050040Z -> 20%. E5's arms select the top 0.5% by predicted tail probability (vol20 is the dominant univariate separator, AUC 0.68/0.78/0.56), so the variance mismatch will be at least as large as for F1_ARA/G2_RET30. With three markets each tested at an effective size of ~15-25%, the family-wise chance of 'Arm B passes in some market' under the null is roughly 40-50%, and the FALSIFIER ('the null is falsified if, in any market, Arm B passes') would be met far too often by noise. The fill-model sensitivity run (same trades, different fills) is highly correlated with the primary and does not restore size. No Bonferroni or per-market correction is declared.

MATCHED CONTROLS ARE OFTEN NOT MATCHED ON VOLATILITY ON IDX AND CRYPTO. controls.py v2 orders keys (price_band, liquidity, market_cap, volatility, momentum, drawdown, listing_age) and relaxes from the last key when fewer than MIN_POOL=5 names match; volatility is a tercile. In the recorded IDX run 000401Z, 291 of 1,042 attempts (28%) were matched on price_band / +liquidity / +market_cap only (match_level_used: 63, 52, 176), i.e. not on volatility at all; crypto 005732Z: 90 of 270 (33%) not matched on volatility; only US matched fully (1,224/1,496). The proposal's central claim 'because the controls match volatility tercile, a ranker that merely picks high-vol names is compared against high-vol names: that is the point' is therefore only partly true on the decisive market (IDX), and a tercile is far coarser than a 0.5% tail. The proposal also forbids any change to controls.py, which removes the obvious fix (a v3 ordering with a finer volatility bucket ahead of market_cap).

ARM B ON IDX IS A REGIME-MISMATCHED LABEL. idxsig/market.py: ARB was 7% flat from 2020-03-13 to 2023-06-05, 15% from 2023-06-05, symmetric with ARA from 2023-09-04. The whole IDX discovery period (2021-01-22..2022-12-30) sits under ARB 7%, where a -23% move in 5 sessions needs >=3-4 consecutive limit-down closes. Computed read-only on the on-disk IDX panel (panel-20261007T225823Z), discovery only, e1-style eligibility: U = 6,076 (1.879%, matches E1), D = 2,185 (0.676%), U&D = 0 (never co-occur), and 1,993 of 2,185 D events (91%) have >=3 lock_down closes in t+1..t+5. So logit_D on IDX is a predictor of ARB-7% lock-down cascades, a mechanism that is partly removed in June 2023 and wholly removed in September 2023, i.e. in the middle of the validation year. The directional score logit_U - logit_D is then fit on one limit regime and validated on three; a pass or fail on IDX Arm B cannot be attributed to T-0 information. (For reference, computed on discovery only: crypto U 5.56% / D 6.19%, US survivor-only U 1.13% / D 1.05%; no such limit artefact there.)

THE CRYPTO FILL-B SENSITIVITY CANNOT RUN AS WRITTEN. execution.execute raises 'fill model B is defined for open entries in as-traded units' unless units='as_traded', and backtest.run raises 'units=as_traded needs a panel with a unit_factor column' (backtest.py:258-261). panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz has no unit_factor column (only panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z does), and no crypto repair panel or build step exists; the E4 branch's crypto protocol also used fill A only. The proposal both requires this sensitivity for any policy consequence and forbids changes to backtest.py/execution.py, so the pre-registered pass rule for crypto is unexecutable.

THE VERDICT RULE CONFLATES INFORMATION WITH EXECUTION. Stage 1 kills an arm on e3.admissibility (scored >= 200, avg net > 0, p < 0.05 vs matched, positive every discovery year), an execution-and-cost criterion under one plan, and the INFO VALUE section then reads 0/3 as 'the whole daily-bar price-only detection family is closed on information grounds, not execution grounds'. A ranker with real direction (directional ratio CI > 1, gross close-to-close r5 above matched) can fail that gate through costs, the 5-session fixed exit, ARA locks or SKIP_LIQUIDITY (F1_ARA: 339 + 248 of 1,042 attempts). The detection-level quantities that would actually test information (AUC_U, AUC_D, directional ratio, pre-move split) are 'reported, not judged'. The proposal's own RISKS admit a null from one L2 rank-logistic 'is not a proof', contradicting the closure claim; and the information set is 15-17 hand-chosen features, not 'the entire daily-bar information set', so 'ceiling' overstates it.

DIRECTIONAL-RATIO BOOTSTRAP IGNORES CLUSTERING. Ranker scores built from vol20, dd60, age, logval20 are persistent, so flags cluster on consecutive sessions of the same name and across names on the same session; a 1000-resample bootstrap over flags treats them as independent and gives CIs that are too narrow. The same persistence, combined with overlap='skip', means ~900 IDX 2023 flags at 0.5% could collapse to a few hundred attempts and, after IDX liquidity/ARA skips (F1_ARA filled 420/1,042), to near or below the scored >= 100 floor; no de-duplication or minimum-attempt rule is pre-registered.

2023 IS ALREADY CONSUMED BY SIBLINGS USING E5'S OWN FEATURES. IDX 2023: E1 F1_ARA (ara) detection + two trading runs; US 2023: E2 G2_RET30 (ret1) + 9 repair reruns + US_BREAKOUT_v1 (brk60); crypto 2023: E2 (ret1) + E4 v2. The univariate 2023 trading outcomes of three E5 inputs (ara, ret1, brk60) and the 2023 r5 medians (-10.3% US, -11.5% crypto, from E2 validation result.json) are known to the designers and motivate the 'variance not direction' thesis and the symmetric D label; the proposal acknowledges the year is once-seen but still writes a FALSIFIER that treats a 2023 pass as falsifying the null. Not fatal for the expected null, but any pass is weak and the closure claim from a consumed year plus a bounded learner is overreach.

CAUSALITY DETAIL: 'features computed as in e1.py Study._signals' is not prefix-safe as written. Study._signals age = arange - first is negative (not NaN) for names not yet listed, and zero20 = rolling sum of present&~tradeable is 0 (not NaN) before listing; in rules.causal_signals the full-window call would rank those rows while the prefix call cannot see them, so per-session rank(pct=True) differs and raises LookaheadError. Must mask by present before ranking (fixable code detail; mentioned because the proposal says 'causal by construction').

VERIFIED (not refuted): gross vs net figures match trades.csv.gz exactly (IDX -3.67%/-4.06%, crypto -1.51%/-1.90%, US -3.19%/-3.65%, US fill B -0.10%/-0.97%); vol20 matched-set AUCs 0.679 IDX / 0.780 US / 0.556 crypto are in the signal_stats.csv files; E1-SIGNALS-v1 / E2-SIGNALS-v1 lists exist in the protocol.json files with the stated exclusions; RULE_FIELDS carries value, lock_up and open; audit.py accepts literal tuples; HEAD cli.py has --holdout-final for IDX only and no US/CRYPTO guard; F1_ARA 2023 flag rate 972/179,617 = 0.54%.
result.fix: Amend KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1 before the protocol is frozen: (1) Replace the primary pass test with one that carries the rule's own variance: per-signal paired difference (rule trade net minus the mean net of its 200 matched controls, obtained in e5.py through execution.execute + controls.matched_draws, the ORACLE path), with a cluster bootstrap over signal sessions (or a date-clustered Welch test); report the harness p alongside but do not judge on it; set the per-market threshold at p < 0.0167 (Bonferroni over the 3 declared primaries) or declare IDX the single primary. (2) Allow one additive controls change: a VERSIONS['v3'] in controls.py with volatility quintile (or decile) ahead of market_cap, so a 0.5% tail is compared with its own volatility stratum; keep v2 reported for comparability. (3) IDX Arm B: define D in limit-relative terms consistent across regimes (e.g. 'min close <= close x prod of (1 - ARB_k) over the next 3 sessions, using the ARB in force at t', or 'locked down on >= 3 of the next 5 sessions'), or restrict the IDX Arm B validation window to 2023-01-02..2023-06-02 and accept the N loss, or drop IDX Arm B and make IDX Arm A the IDX primary with crypto/US Arm B the directional primaries. (4) Crypto sensitivity: pre-register a crypto panel build with unit_factor = 1 (no splits; a stated data step) so fill B can execute, or replace it with fill A at max_participation 0.05 and say so. (5) Split the verdict: an information verdict judged on pre-registered detection statistics (directional ratio cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 1, gross close-to-close r5 of the top 0.5% vs matched) and a separate execution verdict on net trading; drop the 'closes the family on information grounds' wording for a null from one bounded learner. (6) Pre-register a first-entry de-duplication (signal only when a name enters the top 0.5% after being outside it for >= 5 sessions) and the minimum attempt count, and mask age/zero20/all features by present before per-session ranking so the prefix-first check passes. (7) State explicitly that a 2023 pass is non-virgin and that the only consequence is a prospective paper policy, never a holdout touch.
